section_summary: This section documents U.S., British, Japanese, and League of Nations reporting on illicit narcotics manufacture and trafficking centered on Dairen and the Kwantung Leased Territory in 1932–1933. It covers investigations and court dispositions involving George I. Tribe, the Bacri–Takushima group, Jacob Gourevich, several clandestine morphine factories, and Fujita Shokai’s inquiry about cocaine. A lengthy questionnaire describes Kwantung’s narcotics laws, licensing, import-export certificates, inspections, penalties, and opium monopoly, while later documents summarize the year’s narcotics cases and begin a report on the territory’s 1933–1934 budget.

subfiles.title: Report on George I. Tribe's identity and history
subfiles.to: A. A. Elliott, Acting District Supervisor
subfiles.about: Reports the results of an investigation into George I. Tribe's origins, American residence, acquaintances, finances, and possible involvement in narcotics.
subfiles.summary: Kaskel identifies George Tribe as Israel Treibuch, born in Pinsk in 1902, who went from Harbin to San Francisco in 1922; details his work, finances and associates and finds no evidence of US drug trafficking.

subfiles.title: Confidential instruction transmitting information on George I. Tribe
subfiles.about: Transmits a Treasury Department letter and investigative report concerning George I. Tribe.
subfiles.summary: Department forwards confidential Treasury information on Tribe, indicted at Dairen for complicity in narcotics smuggling, following Dairen Despatch 244 of February 2, 1932.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting British information on a secret Japanese morphine factory
subfiles.from: Harry J. Anslinger, Commissioner of Narcotics
subfiles.to: John K. Caldwell, Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits a circular concerning the discovery of a clandestine Japanese morphine factory.
subfiles.summary: Commissioner of Narcotics sends Caldwell a circular on a secret Japanese morphine factory received through international reporting channels.

subfiles.title: Home Office Circular No. 49 on the Kokusekisho morphine factory
subfiles.to: Rotterdam, Paris, Washington, Ottawa, and Cairo authorities
subfiles.about: Reports the discovery near Dairen of a factory that had allegedly produced morphine since November 1931.
subfiles.summary: Home Office Circular 49: Dairen papers reported police found a secret Kokusekisho factory and seized about forty kilograms of morphine; fourteen Japanese suspects named.

subfiles.title: Instruction to investigate the reported Dairen morphine factory
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Orders the consul to report information on the secret morphine factory and similar cases.
subfiles.summary: Department encloses Anslinger's June 3 letter and the British circular and tells Langdon to get information on the Dairen factory and similar cases.

subfiles.title: Telegram requesting outcomes in Dairen narcotics cases
subfiles.about: Requests telegraphic reports on the Bacri–Takushima case and Gourevich's conviction and movements.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks for the result of the Bacri–Takushima case and a copy and translation of the court sentence. It also seeks particulars of Gourevich's reported April conviction and information about his movements or destination. Page 160 contains brief associated notations rather than substantive new correspondence.

subfiles.title: Follow-up telegram requesting a report
subfiles.about: Presses the Dairen consulate for a partial or complete response to earlier narcotics inquiries.
subfiles.summary: Department asks when it may expect the requested report on Dairen narcotics cases.

subfiles.title: Telegram reporting the location of the Gourevich brothers
subfiles.about: Reports that convicted J. Gourevich remained in Dairen while his brother Abramovich was believed to be in Tientsin.
subfiles.summary: Consul: J. Gourevich is in Dairen after conviction; Abramovich Gourevich, believed leader, is in Tientsin; sentence report to follow.

subfiles.title: Notification to Treasury concerning the Gourevich case
subfiles.about: Relays the Dairen consul's report that J. Gourevich was convicted and that his brother was believed to lead the gang.
subfiles.summary: State tells Treasury of the July 11 telegram: sentence details to follow, and Abramovich Gourevich thought to be the gang's leader in Tientsin.

subfiles.title: Observations on Fujita Shokai's cocaine inquiry
subfiles.about: Comments on a League of Nations memorandum concerning Fujita Shokai's request for British cocaine prices.
subfiles.summary: The Department recalls a 1928 seizure at Kobe of 3.09 kilograms of benzoyl-morphine shipped from Dairen by Fujita. It contrasts Japanese claims about legitimate demand with League calculations placing 1930 Kwantung cocaine consumption at ten kilograms. On that basis, it argues that a proposed four-kilogram shipment would be substantial.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Dairen despatch No. 18
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the consul's report on Kwantung narcotics laws and regulations.
subfiles.summary: Department acknowledges Dairen despatch 18 of January 6, 1933 and appreciates the effort on the regulatory summary.

subfiles.title: League of Nations memorandum on Fujita Shokai's cocaine inquiry
subfiles.from: League of Nations Advisory Committee on Traffic in Opium and Other Dangerous Drugs; communicated by the British Representative
subfiles.about: Describes Fujita Shokai's request to May and Baker for the price of four kilograms of cocaine hydrochloride.
subfiles.summary: League memo: May and Baker declined Fujita Shokai's cocaine inquiry without an import certificate; Japan said Hiroharu Fujita wanted market information and four kilograms suited parcel rates, against Kwantung's legitimate demand of about thirty kilograms.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 8: Bacri–Takushima narcotics case
subfiles.about: Reports sentences in the Bacri–Takushima case and details the transactions for which George I. Tribe was convicted.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 8: Judge Oda sentenced Takushima to one year and Bacri to six months, fined Tribe and Lelchitsky, acquitted Bogdanovsky and Granevsky; Tribe traded heroin, benzoline and morphine in 1929-1931 and was likely more than a tool.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of the Bacri–Takushima despatch to Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards despatch No. 8 on the disposition of the case involving Bacri, Takushima, and Tribe.
subfiles.summary: Department sends Treasury Vincent's November 16 report on the Bacri-Takushima defendants for the Commissioner of Narcotics.

subfiles.title: Telegram pressing Dairen for current narcotics reporting
subfiles.about: Orders prompt reporting on Gourevich, court sentences, the morphine factory, and other illicit traffic.
subfiles.summary: Department tells Dairen to keep Washington and Shanghai's Treasury attaché informed by discreet inquiry and to speed replies on court and factory matters, stressing Dairen's role in illicit traffic.

subfiles.title: Instruction enclosing League report on a clandestine factory
subfiles.about: Forwards a League of Nations report on a clandestine drug factory near Dairen and again requests the consul's report.
subfiles.summary: Department encloses League document O.C.S. 82 of December 1, 1932 with Japanese information on a clandestine factory and says it still awaits the consul's response.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to report on expanding opium cultivation in Chōsen
subfiles.about: Directs researchers to another file concerning a proposal to expand Korean opium cultivation for Kwantung.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: report 895.114 Narcotics/18 on increasing opium cultivation in Chōsen so Kwantung could replace Persian supplies.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 11: Jacob Gourevich
subfiles.about: Reports Jacob Gourevich's sentence, whereabouts, and nominal business activity.
subfiles.summary: Vincent reports that Gourevich was fined 100 yen on April 4, 1932, at the same time as Bacri and Takushima. Gourevich remained in Dairen and was nominally engaged in the oil business, but details of his activities were unavailable. Vincent promises to keep Washington and the Treasury attaché informed.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 12: Morphine factory near Dairen
subfiles.about: Reports the investigation, arrests, and sentences arising from the Kokusekisho morphine factory.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 12: police raided a stone morphine factory near Hoshigaura February 10; fourteen suspects, nine received short sentences or small fines; Vincent and his British colleague called them too lenient.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Despatch No. 11 on Jacob Gourevich
subfiles.about: Forwards the Dairen consul's report on Jacob Gourevich to the Commissioner of Narcotics.
subfiles.summary: Department sends Despatch 11 of December 13, 1932 on Jacob Gourevich, suspected of complicity in narcotics traffic.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Despatch No. 12 on the Kokusekisho factory
subfiles.about: Forwards the Dairen consul's report on the illicit factory at Kokusekisho.
subfiles.summary: Department sends Despatch 12 of December 14, 1932 on the Kokusekisho factory with British Circular 49 and League document O.C.S. 82.

subfiles.title: Circular No. 82: Secret morphine factories at or near Dairen
subfiles.to: Cairo, Paris, Ottawa, Rotterdam, and Washington authorities
subfiles.about: Summarizes five press-reported illicit morphine-manufacturing cases in and around Dairen.
subfiles.summary: British Circular 82 on secret Dairen morphine factories: Showa Yoko, a factory exposed by fire, exports to Changchun, arrests and a fatal fire, possible links to Tokyo Seiyaku and Henri Bacri; several investigations unresolved.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 15: Fujita Shokai, Dairen
subfiles.about: Reports an investigation of Fujita Shokai and its proprietors following the firm's cocaine-price inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 15: Fujita Shokai's Dairen and Changchun branches do little business; Yoichi Fujita reportedly speculates in currency and his son Hiroharu runs a brick concern; both have poor reputations.

subfiles.title: Instruction transmitting Circular No. 82 and requesting follow-up reports
subfiles.about: Forwards British information on secret morphine factories as an example of the reporting Washington expects.
subfiles.summary: Instruction sends a British memorandum on Circular 82 under confidential sharing, asks cooperation with the British consul and further reports on the cases.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 18: Reply to narcotics-control questionnaire
subfiles.about: Transmits Kwantung Government answers to a questionnaire on narcotics laws and administration.
subfiles.summary: Vincent explains that the answers were supplied in Japanese and were sometimes incomplete or misunderstood. The separate administration of the opium monopoly and other narcotics complicated the responses. He promises later translations of regulations and ordinances not already sent to Washington.

subfiles.title: Kwantung questionnaire on legal and administrative control of narcotics
subfiles.from: Kwantung Government; transmitted by the American Consulate at Dairen
subfiles.about: Provides a detailed account of Kwantung's narcotics laws, licensing, trade controls, inspections, and penalties.
subfiles.summary: The questionnaire lists the laws controlling opium, morphine, cocaine, ecgonine, and cannabis and identifies the Monopoly Bureau and police as the principal administering bodies. It explains licensing, storage, recordkeeping, prescriptions, import and export certificates, postal shipment, transit, diversion, inspections, confiscation, and penalties. Kwantung is described as a duty-free territory, though narcotics remained regulated, and the answers acknowledge limited centralized reporting and no dedicated narcotics inspectors. It also describes information-exchange arrangements with Britain and the United States.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Despatch No. 15 on Fujita Shokai
subfiles.about: Forwards Vincent's investigation of Fujita Shokai to the Commissioner of Narcotics.
subfiles.summary: Department sends Despatch 15 on Fujita Shokai's Dairen and Changchun operations and proprietors, referring to its August 10, 1932 correspondence.

subfiles.title: Traffic in Narcotics in Kwantung case jacket
subfiles.about: Serves as the physical jacket for a case on narcotics traffic in Kwantung.
subfiles.summary: Case jacket 'Traffic in Narcotics in Kwantung', with instructions not to rearrange papers.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 19: Narcotics cases in Dairen during 1932
subfiles.about: Summarizes eleven principal illicit-narcotics cases handled or reported in Dairen during 1932.
subfiles.summary: Vincent reviews the Kokusekisho and Showa Yoko factories, the Bacri–Takushima case, factory fires, morphine exports to Changchun, crude-morphine arrests, smuggling discoveries, and the Benzoline Case. He identifies defendants, outcomes, unresolved investigations, and legal arguments concerning Ordinance No. 54. Drawing on British assistance, he concludes that light punishments and reluctant investigations seriously weakened narcotics enforcement.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Despatch No. 18 and its regulatory questionnaire
subfiles.about: Sends Treasury the Dairen consulate's summary of Kwantung narcotics laws and regulations.
subfiles.summary: Department sends Treasury Despatch 18 and its regulatory questionnaire, with untranslated regulations to follow.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Despatch No. 18
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the report on narcotics laws in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: Second file copy acknowledging the January 6 despatch and commending the effort in compiling regulatory information.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of the 1932 Dairen narcotics-case summary
subfiles.about: Forwards Despatch No. 19 summarizing Dairen narcotics cases handled during 1932.
subfiles.summary: Department sends Vincent's January 18 summary of illicit-drug cases taken up by Dairen authorities in 1932 for the Commissioner of Narcotics.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of report on the Kwantung Government budget
subfiles.about: Forwards a consular report on Kwantung's 1933–1934 budget, emphasizing opium-monopoly finances.
subfiles.summary: Department sends Treasury a January 16 despatch on the Kwantung Government budget, noting difficulty measuring the opium monopoly's revenue share and a substantial increase in its appropriation.

subfiles.title: Report on the Kwantung Government budget for 1933–1934
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador at Tokyo
subfiles.about: Begins a report comparing Kwantung Government budgets and explaining the proposed increase for fiscal 1933–1934.
subfiles.summary: Kwantung budget for 1933-1934: expenditure of 25,864,792 yen, up 3,128,776, read as real expansion rather than yen compensation; revenue table begins; continues.
